title: Baby Mealtimes: Self-Feeding & First Tastes
strapline: Squish it, smear it, grab it, taste it — mealtimes where the mess is the learning.
intent: Letting babies feed themselves — grasping soft finger foods and scooping with a spoon — builds hand-eye coordination, grip and independence.
Exploring food with hands, mouth and eyes gives babies rich sensory experience of texture, temperature, smell and taste.
Discovering that they can pick up, drop and pick up again is early cause-and-effect and joyful, repeatable control.
Warm, unhurried mealtimes with a familiar adult build security, communication and the pleasure of eating together.
Offering a variety of first tastes, including foods from each baby's home, helps babies accept and enjoy a wide range of flavours.
implementation: Offer safe, soft, graspable finger foods and let babies feed themselves at their own pace, mess and all.
Sit close, follow the baby's cues for more or done, and never hurry or force a taste.
Name what is happening warmly — 'you're holding the banana!', 'that one dropped — here it is again'.
Offer a spoon to hold and explore alongside your own, welcoming every wobbly scoop.
Talk with families about home foods and first tastes, and offer familiar flavours so mealtimes feel safe.
Treat spills and smears as exploration, not misbehaviour, and let the discovery unfold.
key_questions: You're holding the banana all by yourself!
That one dropped — here it is again!
Shall we have some more, or are you all done?
Can you feel how cool the cucumber is?
You're scooping with the spoon — good scooping!

impact.text: Babies feed themselves finger foods and hold their own cup with growing skill.
Babies reach, grasp, transfer and release food, exploring with hands and mouth.
Babies experience texture, temperature, smell and taste with all their senses.
Warm, unhurried mealtimes with a familiar adult build security and co-regulated calm.
Babies meet a variety of first tastes, including flavours from their own home.

enhancements: A spoon to hold and explore alongside the adult's, welcoming every wobbly scoop.
A rotating range of first tastes, including a familiar flavour from each baby's home.
A low mirror by the highchair so babies watch themselves eat.
Textured, safe finger foods — soft, ripe, graspable — offered in an unhurried, mess-welcome way.
A photo of home mealtimes shared with families to keep tastes and routines connected.

playing_exploring: Babies explore food freely with hands and mouth, at their own pace and in their own way.
active_learning: Babies persist at grasping and scooping, dropping and reaching again, delighting in the effort.
creating_thinking: Babies begin to connect their own grasp and scoop to getting the food, and try it another way when it slips.
